_tensor_spec_note: tensor_spec is the input-plane spec each checkpoint was TRAINED under, not the current one. v1 normalizes the distance planes by board_size**2, v2 by 2*board_size — a board_size/2 rescale of channels 8/9 (2.5x at 5x5, 4.5x at 9x9). Loading a model without passing its own spec silently feeds it planes on a scale it never saw. Every 5x5 checkpoint and the v4/v5 9x9 pair predate the v2 switch; the v9/v10 entries are spec 2. Runs record spec_version in the run dir's config.json.

2p_vector.notes: Trained with max^n MCTS (= negamax at N=2), 30 iterations, augmentation + gamma=0.99. 40/40 vs the greedy racer at 200 sims (20 games/seat, tensor spec v1) and plays the seat asymmetry optimally: seat 1 wins in 3 turns with ZERO walls (a pure race — two racers meet head-on and the second jumps the first, gaining a tempo), seat 0 wins in 4 turns with exactly 1 wall, the minimum investment that beats the deficit. Strongest model in the repo. Its gamma=0.97 sibling (runs/n2_5x5_g097_v1) scores 20/40 — identical seat 1, but 0/20 in seat 0 where it over-walls (3/game): a steeper discount suppresses paying a tempo now to win later.

4p_ship.notes: Trained with max^n MCTS, 70 iterations, augmentation + γ=0.99. Peak checkpoint iter 68.

2p_legacy.notes: Original scalar architecture. Trained with negamax MCTS, v3.2 notebook, 40 iterations.

2p_9x9.eval_win_rate: ~97-100% vs random (fair share 50%) BUT 0% vs a greedy pawn-rush
2p_9x9.notes: Full-size 9x9, 10 walls/player. max^n MCTS, 600 sims, γ=0.99. best.pt = accept-gated peak of n2_9x9_v4. NOT DEMO-READY: 0/40 vs the greedy racer on every one of 12 training evals, and 0/12 on a direct per-seat probe at 200 sims (seat 0 and seat 1 both). It spends ~61% of its turns placing walls and loses even the seat where walking forward wins outright. The vs-random number is saturated and hides this — do not quote it alone.

4p_9x9.eval_win_rate: ~88-96% vs random (fair share 25%) BUT 0% vs a greedy pawn-rush
4p_9x9.notes: Full-size 9x9, 5 walls/player. max^n MCTS, 600 sims, γ=0.99. best.pt = accept-gated peak of n4_9x9_v5. NOT DEMO-READY: 0/40 vs the greedy racer on all 14 training evals. Same pathology as 2p_9x9. The vs-random number is saturated — do not quote it alone.

2p_9x9_v9.eval_win_rate: 93.8% pooled vs the greedy racer (iter 12, 80 games): seat 0 39/40, seat 1 36/40
2p_9x9_v9.notes: THE N=2 DELIVERABLE. Full-size 9x9, 10 walls/player, warm-started from runs/pretrain_n2_9x9. First 9x9 model that both races and walls, and the first with BOTH seats over 90%. Identical to that run's ship.pt. Pinned to greedy_peak.pt by path on purpose: the run never accepted in 60 iterations, so best.pt is the untrained initialization, and pooled rate decays to 82% by iter 60. n2_9x9_v10 peaked lower (87.5%, iter 16) and does not replace this.

4p_9x9_v9.eval_win_rate: 40% best-seat (seat 0, 8/20) at the iter-12 peak; pooled ceiling is 25%
4p_9x9_v9.notes: Superseded by 4p_9x9_v10; kept as the record. Peaked at seat 0 8/20 (10% pooled) at iter 12, then the gate ACCEPTED at iters 20/24/28 while the per-seat rate fell to 0%, so best.pt and ship.pt both hold the dead iter-28 model. This run is why the demo pins greedy_peak.pt rather than trusting the accept gate.

4p_9x9_v10.eval_win_rate: 12.5% pooled vs the greedy racer (iter 8, 80 games); seat 0 10/20 = 50%, seats 1-3 0/20
4p_9x9_v10.notes: THE N=4 DELIVERABLE. Full-size 9x9, 5 walls/player, warm-started from runs/pretrain_n4_9x9. Best N=4 result to date — seat 0 at 50% is 6x anything the six pre-warm-start runs managed (none passed 2/80). Pooled 12.5% is below the 25% fair share because only seat 0 ever wins. Identical to that run's ship.pt. Pinned by path: the gate accepted at iter 20, where the racer scores 0/80, so best.pt holds a dead model.

usage.2p_vector: QuoridorModelMP(board_size=5, action_space_size=44, in_channels=9, num_channels=64, num_res_blocks=4, num_players=2)
usage.4p_ship: QuoridorModelMP(board_size=5, action_space_size=44, in_channels=15, num_channels=64, num_res_blocks=4, num_players=4)
usage.2p_9x9: QuoridorModelMP(board_size=9, action_space_size=140, in_channels=9, num_channels=128, num_res_blocks=8, num_players=2)
usage.4p_9x9: QuoridorModelMP(board_size=9, action_space_size=140, in_channels=15, num_channels=128, num_res_blocks=8, num_players=4)

variants._note: Which registry model backs each (board_size, num_players) demo, plus the env settings it was trained under. max_walls matters as much as the weights: the walls-remaining plane is scaled by it, so serving a checkpoint at the wrong wall count feeds it planes it never saw. Read via src/utils/model_registry.py.
variants._wall_candidates_note: The MCTS wall-expansion budget K the checkpoint TRAINED under, and therefore the only K it should be served at — a result scored at a different K is not comparable, and the gap is large: n2_9x9_v7 (trained K=16) scores 80.0% vs greedy at K=16 and 47.5% at K=0. 0 means unrestricted; every 5x5 checkpoint predates the restriction, and 9x9 v8 onward trained at 16 (configs/config_9x9.json mcts_wall_candidates). Serving the wrong K fails silently — the model just plays badly. See docs/restricted_wall_search.md.
variants._max_turns_note: PLIES, not rounds — QuoridorEnvMP increments turn_count once per step, the same unit as max_game_moves in training and max_moves in the evaluator. Each value is the horizon its own run used (runs/<run>/config.json): 150 for both 5x5 runs, 160 at 9x9 N=2 and 320 at 9x9 N=4, set per variant to give every player the same ~80-ply budget. Serving N=4 at a shorter horizon than 320 scores as a timeout the games the measured configuration had room to convert.
